passages.text: Hallelujah! Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.
passages.sermon:
Hallelujah!
Give thanks to the LORD.
The LORD is good.
His loving devotion lasts forever.
passages.original: הַֽלְלוּיָ֨הּ׀ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Who can describe the mighty acts of the LORD or fully proclaim His praise?
passages.sermon: The LORD does mighty acts.\r\nNo one can fully describe His mighty acts.\r\nNo one can fully proclaim all His praise.
passages.original: מִ֗י יְ֭מַלֵּל גְּבוּר֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה יַ֝שְׁמִ֗יעַ כָּל־ תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Blessed are those who uphold justice, who practice righteousness at all times.
passages.sermon: People who uphold justice are blessed.\r\nThey do what is right.\r\nThey practice righteousness at all times.
passages.original: אַ֭שְׁרֵי שֹׁמְרֵ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֑ט עֹשֵׂ֖ה צְדָקָ֣ה בְכָל־ עֵֽת׃

passages.text: Remember me, O LORD, in Your favor to Your people; visit me with Your salvation, that I may see the prosperity of Your chosen ones, and rejoice in the gladness of Your nation, and give glory with Your inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD shows favor to His people.
I ask the LORD to remember me.
I ask the LORD to show me His favor.
I ask the LORD to visit me with His salvation.
I want to see the good things You give to Your chosen ones.
I want to rejoice when Your nation is glad.
I want to give glory together with Your people.
Your people are Your inheritance.
passages.original: זָכְרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה בִּרְצ֣וֹן עַמֶּ֑ךָ פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃ לִרְא֤וֹת׀ בְּט֘וֹבַ֤ת בְּחִירֶ֗יךָ לִ֭שְׂמֹחַ בְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת גּוֹיֶ֑ךָ לְ֝הִתְהַלֵּ֗ל עִם־ נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly.
passages.sermon:
We have sinned.
Our fathers also sinned.
We have done wrong.
We have acted wickedly.
passages.original: חָטָ֥אנוּ עִם־ אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

passages.text: Our fathers in Egypt did not grasp Your wonders or remember Your abundant kindness; but they rebelled by the sea, there at the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
Our fathers lived in Egypt.
They did not understand Your wonders.
They did not remember Your great kindness.
They rebelled against You at the sea.
They rebelled at the Red Sea.
passages.original: אֲב֘וֹתֵ֤ינוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם׀ לֹא־ הִשְׂכִּ֬ילוּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א זָ֭כְרוּ אֶת־ רֹ֣ב חֲסָדֶ֑יךָ וַיַּמְר֖וּ עַל־ יָ֣ם בְּיַם־ סֽוּף׃

passages.text: Yet He saved them for the sake of His name, to make His power known.
passages.sermon: God saved the people of Israel.\r\nHe did this for the sake of His name.\r\nHe wanted everyone to know His power.
passages.original: וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמ֑וֹ לְ֝הוֹדִ֗יעַ אֶת־ גְּבוּרָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; He led them through the depths as through a desert.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power at the Red Sea.
God rebuked the Red Sea.
The Red Sea dried up.
God led the Israelites through the depths.
The depths became like a desert for them.
passages.original: וַיִּגְעַ֣ר בְּיַם־ ס֭וּף וַֽיֶּחֱרָ֑ב וַיּוֹלִיכֵ֥ם בַּ֝תְּהֹמ֗וֹת כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: He saved them from the hand that hated them; He redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power and mercy.
God saved His people.
He rescued them from those who hated them.
He redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
passages.original: וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם מִיַּ֣ד שׂוֹנֵ֑א וַ֝יִּגְאָלֵ֗ם מִיַּ֥ד אוֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: The waters covered their foes; not one of them remained.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
He caused water to cover the enemies of Israel.
None of those enemies survived.
Not a single foe remained.
passages.original: וַיְכַסּוּ־ מַ֥יִם צָרֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד מֵ֝הֶ֗ם לֹ֣א נוֹתָֽר׃

passages.text: Then they believed His promises and sang His praise.
passages.sermon:
The people believed God's promises.
They trusted what God said.
They sang songs to praise God.
They gave thanks to God with their voices.
passages.original: וַיַּאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִדְבָרָ֑יו יָ֝שִׁ֗ירוּ תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Yet they soon forgot His works and failed to wait for His counsel.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel saw God's mighty works.
They quickly forgot what God had done.
They did not wait for God's guidance.
They acted without seeking His counsel.
passages.original: מִֽ֭הֲרוּ שָׁכְח֣וּ מַעֲשָׂ֑יו לֹֽא־ חִ֝כּ֗וּ לַעֲצָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They craved intensely in the wilderness and tested God in the desert.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites traveled in the wilderness.
They wanted things very strongly.
They craved intensely.
They were not satisfied.
They tested God in the desert.
They challenged Him there.
passages.original: וַיִּתְאַוּ֣וּ תַ֭אֲוָה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּוּ־ אֵ֝֗ל בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃

passages.text: So He granted their request, but sent a wasting disease upon them.
passages.sermon: God listened to the people.\r\nHe gave them what they asked for.\r\nHe sent a wasting disease into their souls.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם שֶׁאֱלָתָ֑ם וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח רָז֣וֹן בְּנַפְשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: In the camp they envied Moses, as well as Aaron, the holy one of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people were in the camp.
They envied Moses.
They also envied Aaron.
Aaron was the holy one of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְקַנְא֣וּ לְ֭מֹשֶׁה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה לְ֝אַהֲרֹ֗ן קְד֣וֹשׁ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The earth opened up and swallowed Dathan; it covered the assembly of Abiram.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
The earth opened its mouth.
The earth swallowed Dathan.
The earth covered the assembly of Abiram.
passages.original: תִּפְתַּח־ אֶ֭רֶץ וַתִּבְלַ֣ע דָּתָ֑ן וַ֝תְּכַ֗ס עַל־ עֲדַ֥ת אֲבִירָֽם׃

passages.text: Then fire blazed through their company; flames consumed the wicked.
passages.sermon: Fire burned among their group.\r\nFlames destroyed the wicked people.
passages.original: וַתִּבְעַר־ אֵ֥שׁ בַּעֲדָתָ֑ם לֶ֝הָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט רְשָׁעִֽים׃

passages.text: At Horeb they made a calf and worshiped a molten image.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were at Horeb.
They made a calf.
They used metal to form the calf.
They worshiped this image.
They bowed down to the molten calf.
passages.original: יַעֲשׂוּ־ עֵ֥גֶל בְּחֹרֵ֑ב וַ֝יִּשְׁתַּחֲו֗וּ לְמַסֵּכָֽה׃

passages.text: They exchanged their Glory for the image of a grass-eating ox.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned away from God.
God was their true glory.
They gave up this glory.
They chose an idol instead.
They made an image of an ox.
This ox ate grass.
They worshiped this image instead of God.
passages.original: וַיָּמִ֥ירוּ אֶת־ כְּבוֹדָ֑ם בְּתַבְנִ֥ית שׁ֥וֹר אֹכֵ֥ל עֵֽשֶׂב׃

passages.text: They forgot God their Savior, who did great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and awesome deeds by the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
The people forgot God.
God is their Savior.
God did great things in Egypt.
God did wondrous works in the land of Ham.
God did awesome deeds by the Red Sea.
passages.original: שָׁ֭כְחוּ אֵ֣ל מוֹשִׁיעָ֑ם עֹשֶׂ֖ה גְדֹל֣וֹת בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃ נִ֭פְלָאוֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָ֑ם נ֝וֹרָא֗וֹת עַל־ יַם־ סֽוּף׃

passages.text: So He said He would destroy them— had not Moses His chosen one stood before Him in the breach to divert His wrath from destroying them.
passages.sermon:
God became angry with the people of Israel.
He decided to destroy them.
Moses was God's chosen servant.
Moses stood before God in the gap.
Moses stopped God's anger from destroying the people.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְֽהַשְׁמִ֫ידָ֥ם לוּלֵ֡י מֹ֘שֶׁ֤ה בְחִיר֗וֹ עָמַ֣ד בַּפֶּ֣רֶץ לְפָנָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֥יב חֲ֝מָת֗וֹ מֵֽהַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: They despised the pleasant land; they did not believe His promise.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel rejected the pleasant land.\r\nThey did not believe God's promise.
passages.original: וַֽ֭יִּמְאֲסוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֑ה לֹֽא־ הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ לִדְבָרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They grumbled in their tents and did not listen to the voice of the LORD.
passages.sermon: The people grumbled in their tents.\r\nThey did not listen to the voice of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֵּרָגְנ֥וּ בְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So He raised His hand and swore to cast them down in the wilderness, to disperse their offspring among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.
passages.sermon:
God punished the Israelites for their unbelief and disobedience.
God raised His hand and made a solemn oath.
God swore to bring them down in the wilderness.
God promised to scatter their children among the nations.
God said He would disperse their descendants throughout many lands.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א יָד֣וֹ לָהֶ֑ם לְהַפִּ֥יל א֝וֹתָ֗ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃ וּלְהַפִּ֣יל זַ֭רְעָם בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּ֝לְזָרוֹתָ֗ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: They yoked themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to lifeless gods.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel joined themselves to Baal of Peor.
Baal of Peor was a false god.
The people ate sacrifices.
These sacrifices were offered to lifeless gods.
Lifeless gods have no power or life.
The people turned away from the LORD.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּצָּ֣מְדוּ לְבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר וַ֝יֹּאכְל֗וּ זִבְחֵ֥י מֵתִֽים׃

passages.text: So they provoked the LORD to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
passages.sermon: The people acted in ways that displeased the LORD.\r\nTheir actions made the LORD angry.\r\nA plague broke out among the people.
passages.original: וַ֭יַּכְעִיסוּ בְּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתִּפְרָץ־ בָּ֝֗ם מַגֵּפָֽה׃

passages.text: But Phinehas stood and intervened, and the plague was restrained.
passages.sermon:
Phinehas was a priest of Israel.
Phinehas saw the people sinning.
Phinehas stood up.
Phinehas took action.
Phinehas intervened for the people.
God stopped the plague.
The plague did not continue.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד פִּֽ֭ינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּ֑ל וַ֝תֵּעָצַ֗ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃

passages.text: It was credited to him as righteousness for endless generations to come.
passages.sermon:
God saw what Phinehas did.
God counted Phinehas’s action as righteousness.
God gave this honor to Phinehas.
God made this honor last for all generations.
God made it last forever.
passages.original: וַתֵּחָ֣שֶׁב ל֭וֹ לִצְדָקָ֑ה לְדֹ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: At the waters of Meribah they angered the LORD, and trouble came to Moses because of them.
passages.sermon: The Israelites gathered at the waters of Meribah.\r\nThey angered the LORD there.\r\nBecause of the Israelites, Moses suffered trouble.
passages.original: וַ֭יַּקְצִיפוּ עַל־ מֵ֥י מְרִיבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥רַע לְ֝מֹשֶׁ֗ה בַּעֲבוּרָֽם׃

passages.text: For they rebelled against His Spirit, and Moses spoke rashly with his lips.
passages.sermon: The people rebelled against God's Spirit.\r\nMoses spoke rashly with his lips.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִמְר֥וּ אֶת־ רוּח֑וֹ וַ֝יְבַטֵּ֗א בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃

passages.text: They did not destroy the peoples as the LORD had commanded them, but they mingled with the nations and adopted their customs.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not destroy the peoples.
The LORD had commanded the Israelites to destroy these peoples.
The Israelites mingled with the nations.
The Israelites learned the customs of these nations.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ הִ֭שְׁמִידוּ אֶת־ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה לָהֶֽם׃ וַיִּתְעָרְב֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽ֝יִּלְמְד֗וּ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They worshiped their idols, which became a snare to them.
passages.sermon: The Israelites worshiped idols.\r\nThese idols became a trap for the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־ עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֑ם וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָהֶ֣ם לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel sacrificed their sons to demons.\r\nThey sacrificed their daughters to demons.
passages.original: וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ אֶת־ בְּ֭נֵיהֶם וְאֶת־ בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם לַשֵּֽׁדִים׃

passages.text: They shed innocent blood— the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel killed innocent people.
They killed their own sons and daughters.
They offered their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
They sacrificed them to the idols of Canaan.
The land became polluted with blood.
passages.original: וַיִּֽשְׁפְּכ֨וּ דָ֪ם נָקִ֡י דַּם־ בְּנֵ֘יהֶ֤ם וּֽבְנוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר זִ֭בְּחוּ לַעֲצַבֵּ֣י כְנָ֑עַן וַתֶּחֱנַ֥ף הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ בַּדָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: They defiled themselves by their actions and prostituted themselves by their deeds.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel acted in evil ways.
They defiled themselves by what they did.
They made themselves unclean through their actions.
They turned away from God.
They acted like those who are unfaithful.
They betrayed God by their deeds.
passages.original: וַיִּטְמְא֥וּ בְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּזְנוּ֗ בְּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So the anger of the LORD burned against His people, and He abhorred His own inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD became very angry with His people.
His people are the Israelites.
The LORD hated His own inheritance.
His inheritance means His chosen people, the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֣ף יְהוָ֣ה בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וַ֝יְתָעֵ֗ב אֶת־ נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He delivered them into the hand of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
passages.sermon:
God became angry with His people.
He rejected His own inheritance.
God handed His people over to other nations.
Their enemies hated them.
Their enemies ruled over them.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם בְּיַד־ גּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽיִּמְשְׁל֥וּ בָ֝הֶ֗ם שֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Their enemies oppressed them, and subdued them under their hand.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel had enemies.
These enemies oppressed the people of Israel.
The enemies subdued the people of Israel.
The people of Israel came under the power of their enemies.
passages.original: וַיִּלְחָצ֥וּם אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּכָּנְע֗וּ תַּ֣חַת יָדָֽם׃

passages.text: Many times He rescued them, but they were bent on rebellion and sank down in their iniquity.
passages.sermon:
God rescued His people many times.
They often rebelled against Him.
They followed their own plans.
They continued in their sin.
They sank deeper into their wrongdoing.
passages.original: פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֗וֹת יַצִּ֫ילֵ֥ם וְ֭הֵמָּה יַמְר֣וּ בַעֲצָתָ֑ם וַ֝יָּמֹ֗כּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָֽם׃

passages.text: Nevertheless He heard their cry; He took note of their distress.
passages.sermon: God saw their trouble.\r\nGod listened when they cried out.\r\nGod noticed their suffering.
passages.original: וַ֭יַּרְא בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־ רִנָּתָֽם׃

passages.text: And He remembered His covenant with them, and relented by the abundance of His loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
God made a covenant with His people.
God remembered this covenant.
God showed great loving devotion.
God relented because of His abundant mercy.
passages.original: וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר לָהֶ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ וַ֝יִּנָּחֵ֗ם כְּרֹ֣ב חַסְדּוֹ׃

passages.text: He made them objects of compassion to all who held them captive.
passages.sermon:
God saw His people in captivity.
Their captors held them.
God caused their captors to show them compassion.
God made His people objects of mercy before all who held them.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אוֹתָ֣ם לְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִ֝פְנֵ֗י כָּל־ שׁוֹבֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name, that we may glory in Your praise.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
He has power to save.
We ask Him to save us.
We ask Him to gather us from all nations.
We want to thank His holy name.
We want to praise Him and give Him glory.
passages.original: הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְקַבְּצֵנוּ֮ מִֽן־ הַגּ֫וֹיִ֥ם לְ֭הֹדוֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ לְ֝הִשְׁתַּבֵּ֗חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “Amen!” Hallelujah!
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD deserves blessing.
The LORD exists from everlasting to everlasting.
All the people should say, "Amen."
All the people should praise the LORD.
Hallelujah!
passages.original: בָּר֤וּךְ־ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֪י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל מִן־ הָ֤עוֹלָ֨ם׀ וְעַ֬ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם וְאָמַ֖ר כָּל־ הָעָ֥ם אָמֵ֗ן הַֽלְלוּ־ יָֽהּ׃
